text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The Rodae SA carmaker, a joint venture between a Romanian car manufacturer and South Korea's Daewoo Heavy Industries, changes its name to Daewoo Automobile Romania.
ADEVARUL
- The monthly inflation rate was 2.4 percent in September, the National Statistics Board reported.
- Former tennis star turned businessman Ion Tiriac denied local media reports that he was interested in buying into troubled private Banca Dacia Felix SA bank.
- The leu currency close to 5,000 to the dollar rate at retail shops in the Transylvanian town of Sibiu.
TINERETUL LIBER
- The Armonia SA investment fund said units rose by 2.26 percent this week, the week's largest rise in investment funds' units.
AZI
- Authorities in the Danube port town of Braila about to conclude an association accord with Shell Romania on the creation of three petrol stations.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Romania opened a privatisation information office in Tel Aviv in a bid to attract foreign investors to its mass selloff.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Romania and Russia will sign an accord in Moscow on Thursday on the expansion of gas transit capacity.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The Romanian IRSOP polling institute and Germany's INFAS will conduct exit poll on November 3 general elections and announce results on Romanian state television.
- Gyorgy Frunda, presidential candidate of the Hungarian Democratic Union (UDMR), said that after the polls UDMR would join a democratic coalition, to take Romania out of the crisis.
- The mayors of six Bucharest districts demanded that the capital city's prefect be sacked over alleged frauds in designating presiding judges for Bucharest's polling stations.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Romania's opposition parties will sign a protocol on Monday to prevent frauds at the November 3 polls.
- The opposition Democratic Convention (CDR) bloc accused the National Broadcasting Committee (CNA) of censorship by suspending the live broadcast of a recent CDR conference.
ADEVARUL
- President Ion Iliescu, campaigning in the southern city of Craiova, took the backdoor exit of the city's main theatre building amid boos by local youths.
- President Iliescu said the opposition CDR was paying up to 40,000 lei a day and the Social Democratic Union (USD) up to 60,000 lei per person to stage protest rallies against him.
JURNALUL NATIONAL
- Interview with heart surgeon Ioan Pop de Popa, presidential candidate of the National centre Union (UNC).
CRONICA ROMANA
- Private television Tele 7 abc will broadcast live Paris horse races on Thursday and Sunday. Romanians will be able to bet with local bookmakers.
LIBERTATEA
- Telephone bills of Romania's central bank and the CNA broadcast media watchdog rose sharply over the past few months due to calls to erotic telephone lines, ROMTELECOM telephone operator said.

- The newspaper analyses the results of the latest three opinion polls which show the opposition CDR poised to win the parliamentary elections and President Iliescu heading to a run-off in the presidential race. ($=3,332 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
